obsidian-second-brain: AI second brain for Obsidian - persistent memory for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Grok Bot

Your AI second brain for Obsidian. Free, open source, and plain Markdown you own.
Talk to Claude as usual. It saves what matters to your vault and remembers it next time.

Install · See it work · All commands · Crew · FAQ · Changelog

Free newsletter: what I learn building this, 3 posts a week. Subscribe to The AI Operator →

**Claude forgets you when a chat ends. Your Obsidian vault doesn't.** This skill connects the two, so every chat adds to one set of linked notes that the next chat reads. - **Save.** `/obsidian-save` turns a chat into linked notes: people, projects, decisions and tasks. - **Feed it.** `/obsidian-ingest` takes a link, PDF, Word file, voice memo or screenshot. It updates the notes you already have instead of piling up new ones. - **Find.** `/obsidian-find` answers from your own notes, with the context around each hit. - **Push back.** `/obsidian-challenge` checks a plan against your past decisions. - **Work while you sleep.** Optional scheduled agents fix contradictions, link lonely notes and write your morning brief. Your notes stay as Markdown files on your computer. The core commands need no API keys. ## See it work


Save a chat, feed it a PDF, and Claude remembers. Animated walkthrough of a made-up example. Real terminal footage →

## Quick start Inside any Claude Code session, run: ``` /plugin marketplace add eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain /plugin install obsidian-second-brain@obsidian-second-brain ``` Then tell Claude where your vault is. Add this to the `env` section of `~/.claude/settings.json`: ```json "env": { "OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH": "/path/to/your/vault" } ``` Restart Claude Code and run `/obsidian-second-brain:obsidian-init` inside your vault. Start with three commands: `obsidian-init` to set up, `obsidian-save` to capture and `obsidian-find` to recall. No vault yet, another AI tool, or bare command names? See the [full install guide](#install). **On Grok Bot?** Start with one prompt and no install: [GROK-BOT.md](GROK-BOT.md).

If this helps you, a star helps other people find it.

An evolution of Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern: a vault that rewrites itself.
Every source updates the pages you already have, not only adds new ones. How it differs →

Powered by Open Knowledge Metabolism (OKM): each fact is timeless, dated, or a pointer. Your notes never fill with facts that used to be true.

--- ## The Problem You use Claude every day. Every session starts from scratch. You re-explain everything. The conversation ends. Everything disappears. Claude Code has no persistent memory across sessions - and neither does Grok Bot, Codex, Gemini, or any of the others. You take notes in Obsidian. Hundreds of files. They just sit there. You make the same decision twice because you forgot you made it six months ago. Ideas rot in daily notes. Nobody connects the dots. **Two powerful tools. Completely disconnected.** You already have the long-term memory. The thing doing the thinking cannot reach it. --- ## Who builds this I'm Eugeniu Ghelbur, an AI automation engineer. I built this for my own vault, and I still run my work on it every day. I review and merge every change myself, and close to 50 people have shipped fixes so far ([see who](#contributors)). I write up what I learn 3 times a week on [The AI Operator](https://theaioperator.io/subscribe?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=who-builds-this), and post shorter notes on [X](https://x.com/eugeniu_ghelbur) and [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eugeniu-ghelbur/). Not a coder? [The Vault](https://theaioperator.io/s/vault?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=vault) has 7 ready-made AI tools for paid readers, including Claude memory and an Obsidian folder set up for AI. Each one takes 10 minutes or less, with no code. --- ## How this extends Karpathy's LLM Wiki Karpathy's pattern is brilliant. Drop sources, LLM creates wiki pages, ask questions. This skill takes it further: | | Karpathy's LLM Wiki | obsidian-second-brain | |---|---|---| | **New sources** | Append new pages, cross-reference | **Rewrite existing pages.** People get updated, claims revised, stale facts replaced. | | **Contradictions** | Flagged, you resolve manually | `/obsidian-reconcile` resolves them automatically | | **Patterns** | Surface when you ask | `/obsidian-synthesize` finds unnamed patterns and writes synthesis pages on its own | | **When it runs** | On demand, when you prompt | 4 scheduled agents: morning brief, nightly consolidation, weekly review, vault-health check | | **Note format** | Human-readable wiki pages | AI-first: `## For future agent` preamble + frontmatter for LLM retrieval, not human review | If Karpathy's wiki is a knowledge base you maintain with an LLM, this is a knowledge base that maintains itself. --- ## What Happens When You Install This **After a meeting:** `/obsidian-save` Claude pulls out every decision, person, task, and idea and saves each one to the right note. You do nothing. **You recorded a voice memo:** `/obsidian-ingest meeting.m4a` Claude transcribes it with a local Whisper install, attributes speakers where the transcript makes them identifiable, extracts every promise and action item, and distributes across entity pages, task boards, and the daily note. **You screenshot a whiteboard:** `/obsidian-ingest photo.png` Claude reads the image, extracts text and structure, creates concept notes, links to related projects. A photo becomes knowledge. **You have a finished text document:** `/obsidian-ingest report.docx` Word (`.docx`, `.doc`) and OpenDocument (`.odt`) files uploaded or copied into the vault follow the same local-source rules as PDFs and Markdown. The helper converts a private copy to a temporary PDF, then ingestion uses the existing PDF path. Text and figures use that path; comments and revision markup are excluded. The original stays unchanged and remains the source under the existing provenance rules. Requires Python 3.10+ and [LibreOffice 26.2+](https://www.libreoffice.org/download/download-libreoffice/), installed separately. Run `python scripts/document_to_pdf.py "path/to/report.docx"`; it prints the PDF path. Put `soffice` on PATH or add `--soffice` with its executable path (Windows: `C:/Program Files/LibreOffice/program/soffice.com`; macOS: `/Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice`). Remove the generated PDF and its temporary parent folder after capture. No additional Python packages are needed. See [the ingest command](commands/obsidian-ingest.md). Presentation and spreadsheet formats remain outside scope. **You find a great video:** `/obsidian-ingest https://youtube.com/...` Claude doesn't summarize into one note. It REWRITES your existing pages. People get updated. Contradictions get resolved. Patterns trigger new synthesis pages. One URL in. The vault is smarter. **Before a big decision:** `/obsidian-challenge` Claude searches your vault for past failures and reversed decisions on the same topic. Pushes back with your own words. Your vault holds you accountable. **You want to see the big picture:** `/obsidian-visualize` Claude generates a visual canvas of your entire vault. Hub nodes centered, color-coded by type, orphans highlighted. Open it in Obsidian and see the shape of your knowledge. **You go to sleep:** The nightly agent runs 5 phases: closes the day, reconciles contradictions, synthesizes cross-source patterns, heals orphan notes, and rebuilds the index. You wake up to a smarter vault. **You start a new day:** `/obsidian-daily` Claude pulls your calendar events, overdue tasks, and overnight changes into today's note. Your morning starts informed. **Someone shares an X post:** `/x-read https://x.com/...` Grok with live X access fetches the post, the thread, and the replies. Returns verbatim text + TL;DR + key claims + reply sentiment + voices to watch. Returns 3-5 emerging themes (with rep posts + key voices), gaps nobody is filling, hook formats that are working, and 3 specific post ideas you could write today. **You need real research:** `/research "AI memory tools"` Perplexity Sonar Pro pulls a deep dossier with citations: summary, key facts (every claim with a recency marker and source domain), timeline, key players, contrarian views, recommended further reading, open questions. Saved to your vault, auto-opens in Obsidian. **You want vault-first deep research:** `/research-deep "AI memory tools"` Scans your vault for what you already know. Identifies gaps. Spawns 3-5 targeted searches via Perplexity (web) and Grok (X discourse). Synthesizes a delta report: what's new, what's confirmed, contradictions to resolve, recommended vault updates. Vault baseline doesn't get re-researched. Only gaps get filled. **You hit a great YouTube video:** `/youtube https://youtu.be/...` Free transcript via youtube-transcript-api. releases.name: v0.20.0 - The Batch
releases.body:
### Added

- **Resumable directory ingestion (#329, by @2Obe).** `/obsidian-ingest` accepts mixed collections of text, PDFs, audio, and images in bounded sequential batches. It reuses existing extraction, raw deduplication, routing, and approval rules. A small helper appends one hidden completion comment per processed source version to the existing operation log. Repeating the command skips completed unchanged sources and retries unfinished work using existing captures. No start records, attempt IDs, persistent error/approval states, or locking are introduced. First Brain warm start is a directory-ingestion use case; no new command or progress file is introduced.

- **Word/OpenDocument text ingestion through PDF conversion (#353, by @2Obe).** `/obsidian-ingest` accepts `.docx`, `.doc`, and `.odt` through the stdlib-only `scripts/document_to_pdf.py` helper, following the existing local-source and PDF ingestion rules. LibreOffice 26.2+ is required separately. Conversion uses a private copy and profile, excludes comments and revision markup, and prints a temporary PDF path. releases.name: v0.19.0 - The Check-In
releases.body:
### Added

- **`/obsidian-checkin` asks you whether old notes still hold.** A fact check compares notes with notes, so news that never reached the vault (a bill settled, a move, a new job) left a note stale and no lint could see it. Check-in asks the owner: up to 3 people or project notes a day whose facts are older than 14 days, family and active projects first. Each card shows the note's name, the date of its facts, and 1 to 3 facts from the note. "Same" stamps a new `last-checked` field; news rewrites the stale claim and propagates; "skip" asks again after 14 days. The open questions live in `<vault>/.checkin.json`, not in the chat, so a host that drops an unanswered question after an hour re-sends the full cards on its next run until they are answered. `scripts/checkin.py` does the picking, the queue and the rendering, so every host sends the same short message. Opt a note out with `checkin: never`, or move it up with `checkin: priority`.
- **`scripts/check_notes.py` gives hook-less agents the write-time check.** Claude Code checks every vault write through `hooks/validate-ai-first.sh`; Grok Bot, cron agents and scripts that patch files directly were never checked. The new scr

releases.name: v0.18.1
releases.body:
### Fixed

- **`move_note` could swap the contents of two notes in a cloud-synced vault (#324, reported by @jeonpapa, by @tonydzi).** The MCP `move_note` created the destination with `os.link(src, dst)` and then unlinked the source, so for a moment both paths were one file. OneDrive, Dropbox and iCloud track files by identity, and on OneDrive a sync pass in that window left the moved note and an existing note with a similar name in the destination folder holding each other's contents, while the move reported success. The destination is now a new file created with `os.open(dst, O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_WRONLY)`, so "never overwrite an existing destination" stays one atomic syscall with no TOCTOU window. The bytes are written, fsynced and read back through the same descriptor, and the source is removed only if it still holds what was copied, so an edit saved mid-move fails the move instead of being lost. The source's mode and timestamps are copied over. A failed write removes the half-made destination only if it is still the file the move created, and an unreadable source now returns an error instead of raising. A test in `tests/test_mcp_codex_parity.py` checks the two inodes at the mom

releases.name: v0.18.0 - Crew
releases.body:
v0.18.0 adds Crew: 1 shared logbook for 4 agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Bot). Codex finishes a job, you open Claude Code, and it already knows what changed.

## The problem Each AI agent you use starts blind to what the others did. So you paste the same context into every chat, again and again. The agents don't share a memory, and they can't learn from each other's mistakes. ## What Crew does - **One line per job.** After every job, an agent writes one line to a plain markdown file: `18:40 | codex | brand | Astra pass, 0 errors`. - **Instant reads.** Before an agent answers, its own hooks hand it the lines the others added since it last looked. You don't paste anything. - **Lessons you approve.** When one agent checks another's work, it can leave a lesson or name a gap. A lesson becomes a rule in that agent's rules file only when you run `keep`. It works in any plain folder, such as `~/crew`. If you use Obsidian, you can put it in `wiki/team/` inside your vault instead

releases.name: v0.17.0 - The Neighbors
releases.body:
### Added

- **A session running beside another Obsidian plugin is now told which schema governs its writes (#300).** Claude Code merges hook entries instead of replacing them: "Hook entries merge across settings levels", "All matching hooks run in parallel", and "A plugin's or skill's copy of the same handler stays separate" ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)). SessionStart adds every hook's stdout to context, so a second vault plugin's rules arrive alongside ours and the session holds two folder maps and two frontmatter schemas for one vault. Nothing errored and nothing said so: the validator still passed our writes, and the vault drifted into mixed conventions one note at a time. `scripts/vault_plugin_scan.py` reads the SessionStart entries in `~/.claude/settings.json`, a project's `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`, and every installed plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` (found through `installed_plugins.json`), and reports the vault-related ones that are not ours. Follow along

Two posts a week on AI second-brain systems, vault patterns, and what works in practice.

How It Works

  +------------------------------------------+
  |                                          |
  |   LAYER 1: Operations (32 commands)      |
  |   Claude remembers everything            |
  |                                          |
  +------------------------------------------+
  |                                          |
  |   LAYER 2: Thinking Tools (9 commands)   |
  |   Claude thinks with you                 |
  |                                          |
  +------------------------------------------+
  |                                          |
  |   LAYER 3: Context Engine (1 command)    |
  |   Claude knows who you are               |
  |                                          |
  +------------------------------------------+
  |                                          |
  |   LAYER 4: Research Toolkit (7 commands) |
  |   Claude pulls knowledge in              |
  |                                          |
  +------------------------------------------+
  |                                          |
  |   ALWAYS ON                              |
  |   Background agent + 4 scheduled agents  |
  |   Auto-synthesis + save reminders        |
  |                                          |
  +------------------------------------------+

49 commands total. The calendar command (/obsidian-calendar) is Claude Code only (needs the Google Calendar MCP), so the Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Hermes / Pi / Agent Skills builds ship 48.

Layer 1 saves, organizes, ingests, reconciles, exports, schedules your calendar, and maintains your vault. Layer 2 challenges your ideas, surfaces hidden patterns, bridges unrelated domains, and graduates ideas into projects. Layer 3 loads your identity and current state so every session picks up where the last one ended. Layer 4 pulls live external knowledge into the vault: X posts, X trends, web research with citations (key-less by default), YouTube and podcast transcripts. Vault-first synthesis knows what you already know. Always On keeps the vault alive without you lifting a finger.

49 Commands

Operations -- Claude remembers

Command What it does
/obsidian-save Saves everything from the conversation -- decisions, tasks, people, ideas
/obsidian-ingest Ingest a URL, file, or resumable folder batch (text, PDFs, .docx/.doc/.odt via LibreOffice, audio, images). The vault REWRITES itself. 5-15 pages touched per source.
/obsidian-synthesize Auto-finds patterns across sources and writes synthesis pages
/obsidian-reconcile Finds contradictions and resolves them. The vault maintains its own truth.
/obsidian-checkin Asks you whether old people and project notes still hold. Shows what each says, re-asks until you answer, saves the news.

The Vault is Alive

Traditional vaults are filing cabinets. You put things in. They sit there.

This vault rewrites itself with every input:

  • Ingest a source -- existing pages get rewritten, contradictions resolved, patterns synthesized
  • Save a conversation -- entities, concepts, and decisions distribute across the vault
  • Ask a question -- the Two-Output Rule means every answer also updates pages
  • A fact changes -- bi-temporal facts track when it was true AND when the vault learned it. "You believed X on Tuesday. After ingesting Y on Wednesday, you shifted to Z." Full audit trail.
  • Do nothing -- background agent and scheduled agents maintain it while you sleep
  • Wait a week -- auto-synthesis finds cross-source patterns and writes connection pages

The vault after a week is fundamentally different from the vault you started with.

The maintenance layer has a name: OKM (Open Knowledge Metabolism). Storage is the easy half; keeping stored knowledge true is the hard half, and it is where this project spends its effort. OKM is the open spec behind that: every stored fact must be timeless, dated, or a pointer. Slow-changing knowledge (how things work, decisions, ownership) is stored; fast-changing facts (counts, statuses, balances) are linked to where they live with an as of stamp, never copied in to rot. The rule is a one-page spec (references/freshness-policy.md), enforced by a linter (scripts/freshness_lint.py) that /obsidian-health runs. It is the companion to OKF (Google's Open Knowledge Format), and the division is sharper than format-versus-freshness: OKF v0.2 added fields for recording that something went stale (status, stale_after, verified), but a field cannot stop a note claiming "the pipeline has 13 deals" with no stamp on it. OKM is the rule about what may be stored bare at all, and a linter that fails the build when it is not. One spec, one reference linter, no second implementation yet. It is storage-agnostic: any folder of markdown an AI maintains, not just Obsidian vaults.

Background Agent & Scheduled Agents

Background: fires after every context compaction. You keep working. The vault updates itself.

PostCompact -> obsidian-bg-agent.sh -> claude -p (headless) -> vault updated

What arming it costs. The headless run uses --dangerously-skip-permissions, because nobody is there to approve each write. That is why the agent ships inert and stays opt-in. Its tool surface is restricted with --tools "Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep" (the flag that removes every other built-in tool, not just pre-approves these) and no MCP servers are loaded, so it cannot run shell commands or reach the network, and it only adds and updates - it never deletes or merges. If that trade is not one you want, leave it off; every other command works without it.

Scheduled:

Agent When What
morning 8 AM Daily note + overdue tasks
nightly 10 PM Sleeptime consolidation: close day + reconcile + synthesize + heal orphans
weekly Fridays 6 PM Weekly review
health Sundays 9 PM Vault health audit

Save reminders: Claude nudges you to /obsidian-save after 10+ exchanges or when you say "done" or "thanks". No lost conversations.

Bounded recall (opt-in): on every prompt, a UserPromptSubmit hook injects a small brief of the most relevant vault notes - max 4 notes, ~900 chars - or nothing at all when confidence is low (abstention beats noise). Read-only, fail-closed, and every inject/abstain decision is logged to <vault>/.claude-runs/ for audit. Ships inert; arm it with OBSIDIAN_RECALL_ENABLED=1 per hooks/recall.hook.example.json.

Vault Architecture

Starting with personal notes? /obsidian-init offers an optional First-Brain wiki-style variant for an existing, evolving collection of human notes. Human notes live in the First-Brain/ folder, immutable ingestion captures in raw/, and AI-maintained knowledge in wiki/. Initialization ensures the First-Brain/ source folder exists and configures ownership and routing; it does not move or ingest notes. Then use /obsidian-ingest on an individual First Brain file or the collection. Original notes stay in place under instruction-based protection, not a filesystem sandbox. See the initialization command for the full procedure.

Importing a collection? /obsidian-ingest Sources/ --preview discovers eligible text files, PDFs, audio, and images without reading source bodies or writing progress. /obsidian-ingest Sources/ --batch-size 10 processes up to ten sources sequentially through the existing ingestion workflow. Repeat the same command for the next batch or after an interrupted session has stopped; completed unchanged sources are skipped, and unfinished sources reuse their raw captures. Sensitive-content rules and rewrite approvals still apply. Required pending or declined approvals never count as completion.

Progress uses one hidden completion comment per processed source version in existing Logs/YYYY-MM-DD.md files, or legacy log.md; there is no separate state file or additional readable status line. The comment contains the source path, byte hash, raw reference, and timestamp. Each source finishes its catalog, daily-note, and normal log updates before the comment is written. Unfinished work has no completion comment and is retried on the next run; errors and pending approvals appear in the normal report. Removing completion history requires reprocessing, with raw deduplication retained. Run only one folder ingestion per vault at a time; this minimal helper does not track active sessions, enforce locking, or validate semantic extraction quality. See the ingestion procedure for supported extensions, provenance hashes, custom routing, and recovery. First Brain warm start is simply /obsidian-ingest First-Brain/; other layouts and source collections use the same workflow. Binary originals remain untouched; captures retain existing transcripts, PDF extracts, or image descriptions rather than archive binaries.

Two layouts are supported. scripts/bootstrap_vault.py builds the Obsidian-style layout by default: Daily/, People/, Projects/ and the preset's topic folders such as Goals/ and Mentions/, as laid out in references/vault-schema.md. Pass --style wiki for the wiki-style layout below. A preset folder the wiki layout renames moves to that name (People/ to wiki/entities/, Ideas/ and Knowledge/ to wiki/concepts/); one it does not rename keeps its own name under wiki/ (Goals/ to wiki/goals/, Sources/ to wiki/sources/), so a preset builds the same vault in either layout.

Wiki-style -- LLM-first

Claude is the reader and writer. The vault is a database.

vault/
+-- _CLAUDE.md          # Operating manual
+-- index.md            # Page catalog (Claude reads FIRST)
+-- log.md              # Activity timeline
+-- SOUL.md             # Your identity
+-- CRITICAL_FACTS.md   # ~120 tokens, always loaded (timezone, manager, location)
+-- raw/                # IMMUTABLE source material
+-- wiki/               # Claude's workspace
|   +-- entities/       # People, companies, tools
|   +-- concepts/       # Ideas, frameworks, synthesis
|   +-- projects/       # Project notes
|   +-- daily/          # Daily notes
|   +-- logs/           # Work session logs
|   +-- reviews/        # Weekly/monthly reviews
|   +-- tasks/          # Task notes
|   +-- decisions/      # ADRs
+-- boards/             # Kanban boards
+-- templates/          # Note templates

The user-obsidian-second-brain MCP server (already connected in Grok Bot) provides the vault I/O layer via obsidian_* tools (obsidian_search, obsidian_read_note, obsidian_save_note, obsidian_update_note, obsidian_validate_note, etc.). Skills tell the agent which MCP tool to call and how to structure the data. Set $OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH to your vault root. No hooks, no scheduled agents - Grok Bot has no hook runtime.

Grok Bot can write a live Page, such as a report, a dashboard, or a plan. The Page opens from a card in the chat, stays in the bot's Library, and you can share it with only you, your team, or anyone with the link. A weekly review or a project dashboard from your vault fits this.

On an iPhone 15 Pro or later, pressing and holding the Action Button starts a voice chat with Grok Bot. You need Grok Bot 1.16 or later, and you set it in iPhone Settings > Action Button > Shortcut. Use it to speak a thought and save it into the vault.

Run on Hermes / open models

The skill is model-agnostic. The OpenCode build (and the Codex / Gemini builds) are plain instruction files, so they run on whatever model the host CLI is pointed at - including open models like Nous Research Hermes. No separate build, no code changes. You set the model on OpenCode's side.

There is also a dedicated Hermes Agent build that emits the commands as native Hermes skills (skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md, agentskills.io-compatible), so Hermes discovers and runs them through its own Skills System rather than via a host CLI:

bash scripts/build.sh --platform hermes
# then follow dist/hermes/INSTALL.md (copy into ~/.hermes/skills/ or add as a tap)

Do not run hermes plugins install on this repo's URL. The repo root is not a Hermes plugin (it has no plugin.yaml), and Hermes reports success anyway while registering nothing (#298). Use the skills build above.

This is the skill/playbook half of the Hermes work; the bounded vault-data half is the MCP connector. Native cron and lifecycle-hook integration are tracked in (README truncated)

aiSummary.oneLiner: A structured methodology and configuration set for building a robust 'Second Brain' knowledge base in Obsidian.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Obsidian Second Brain provides a comprehensive template and methodological framework for organizing personal knowledge using the Obsidian application. It implements established knowledge management concepts, such as PARA (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives), structuring the vault for optimal information retrieval and linking. The repository includes pre-configured folders, templates, and plugin recommendations designed to minimize setup time and maximize productivity. It transforms a blank Obsidian installation into a highly organized, interconnected digital workspace for managing complex research and personal data.
keyFeatures: PARA method implementation: Structures the vault logically into Projects, Areas, Resources, and Archives for clear organization.
Pre-configured templates: Includes ready-to-use templates for daily notes, project planning, and reading summaries.
Plugin recommendations: Curates a list of essential Obsidian plugins that enhance the Second Brain methodology.
Interconnected architecture: Promotes robust bi-directional linking strategies to build a highly networked knowledge graph.
Streamlined onboarding: Provides a fully structured starting point to eliminate the friction of configuring a new Obsidian vault.
